In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in MDR-TB was due to the increased proportion of HIV infected individuals, who were more likely to be infected with MDR-TB.
there was an increase in the number of patients who were infected with multidrug resistant TB.
the emergence of MDRTB in New York City was due primarily to transmission from patients with immunocompetent hosts to those with HIV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increase in MDR tuberculosis in New York city during 1987 to 1988 and 1989 to 1990 was due to an increased number of patients with HIV and to the transmission of M tuberculosis from HIV negative to HIV positive patients.
HIV infection and M. tuberculosis transmission are important factors in the emergence of MDR-TB.

the increase in MDRTTB in New York City was due to a combination of factors: the emergence of HIV infection in the city; the increased proportion of TB patients who were HIV infected, and the increased proportion of HIV infected TB patients who had MDRTB; and the increased transmission of MDRTB from HIV seronegative to HIV infected persons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV is an important factor in the transmission of MDR TB.
the increase in MDR TB in New York City is due primarily to reactivation in patients who are HIV infected.
the HIV pandemic has changed the epidemiology of TB in NYC, and that the HIV pandemic will continue to change the epidemiology of MDR-TB in NYC and elsewhere.
